clue.text: Runner impressing club in contest

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so the club is pushed inside the runner

parts.note: a river runs, and the Dee is a British river, a crossword favourite
a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: An athlete brings a club into a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete but is a river, the usual crossword sense; 'impressing' puts the club inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal argument between sides, a verbal contest.

clue.text: US politician having arrived, standing to enter oath

indicators.note: to enter says this piece goes inside the oath

parts.note: drat is a mild oath or curse

indicators.note: standing in a down clue means the word is upright, read from bottom to top

parts.note: come means arrived, in the sense of having come

explanation.surface: An American politician arrives and swears an oath on taking office.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of one of the two main US political parties.

clue.text: Newspaper cutting exposed prolonged attack

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the newspaper divides the other word

parts.note: bare means exposed or uncovered
rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A press cutting exposes a long campaign of attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper cutting' looks like a clipping; here the newspaper cuts into BARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is sustained artillery fire, or by extension any prolonged onslaught.

clue.text: Old communication from, perhaps, plane or jumbo?

definitions.text: Old communication from, perhaps, plane or jumbo?

parts.words: Old communication from, perhaps, plane or jumbo?
parts.note: a plane is a kind of tree and a jumbo an elephant, both with a trunk; old long-distance phone links also had this name

explanation.surface: A dated message sent from an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane or jumbo' suggests aircraft; really a plane tree and an elephant, each owning a trunk. A long-distance phone call was once called this in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Before direct dialling, a long-distance phone call routed over trunk lines had this name.

clue.text: Individual entering appeal, an official in authority

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: charm is attractiveness or appeal
I is the Roman numeral one, a single individual
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person lodging an appeal turns out to be a figure of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman presides over a meeting or board, an official holding authority.

clue.text: A scold's bridle would shut up

explanation.walkthrough: A scold's bridle was a medieval punishment device fitted over the head with a plate pressing down the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scold's bridle was an iron mask that clamped the tongue; the phrase also means to stay silent.

clue.text: Drunkard won't start on very strong pot

indicators.note: won't start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a wino is a drunkard
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud or strong

explanation.surface: An alcoholic refuses to begin on very strong cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: An in-off is a snooker or billiards pot where the cue ball goes into the pocket off another ball; 'pot' is not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards, an in-off is a shot where the cue ball enters a pocket after striking another ball, a kind of pot.

clue.text: Insect numbers on the rise, one running wild

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the rise means the whole run is read upwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small flying insect
a sum is a set of numbers added

explanation.surface: Insect counts are increasing as one runs amok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' reverses the whole of GNATSUM, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: For rugby players the end is up, having packed swelling

indicators.note: having packed means holding inside, so the swelling contains the other piece

parts.note: a node is a small swelling or lump

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

explanation.surface: Rugby players see the game is over and pack a swollen limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' turns the little word is upwards before it is packed. No-side is the old rugby term for full time.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, no-side is the referee's call ending the match.

clue.text: So calm and euphoric, out of one's tiny mind!

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone so calm and happy seems mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of one's mind' looks like the definition; 'out' is the anagram signal and 'and' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Microcephalous means having an abnormally small head, hence a tiny brain.

clue.text: Bandicoot, perhaps, wrecking puma's lair

indicators.note: wrecking the lair smashes its letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A small animal wrecks a big cat's den.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot is an Australian pouched mammal, one example of the group.

clue.text: Group seeking refuge

explanation.definitionFit: Oasis was a 1990s British rock band; a desert oasis is a place of refuge and refreshment.

clue.text: Beautiful woman pulled at Christmas?

explanation.surface: A man pulls an attractive woman at a Christmas party.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a British party novelty two people pull until it snaps; 'pulled' also hints at romantic success.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracker is British slang for an attractive woman, and a Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled apart at the festive table.

clue.text: Casual worker poor at first

indicators.note: at first places the word for poor ahead of the worker

parts.note: food that has gone off is poor or bad
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A temporary labourer is no good at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual and unconcerned, the same easy-going sense.

clue.text: Ring department to claim compensation, finally

indicators.note: to claim means to take in, so the department holds the letter

parts.note: an area is a field or department of activity

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word compensation

explanation.surface: A department ring-fences money to pay compensation claims.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for contests, like a boxing or circus ring.

clue.text: Possible Great Rift Valley?

parts.note: the African rift valley is pictured as a vast gap between two rises, the kind of line seen in a low neckline

explanation.surface: A geography question about an African valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about African geology; the cryptic reading pictures the deep gap between a woman's breasts. Cleavage is also the geological term for splitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleavage means a split or division, and also the hollow shown by a low-cut top.

clue.text: Quit injecting carbon: popular so to prevent disease

indicators.note: injecting means putting into, so the pieces go inside the word for quit

parts.note: vacate means to quit or leave a place
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Instructions to inject a popular carbon compound against disease.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaccinate is to give a vaccine that protects against infection.

clue.text: Instrument to take in with blood screening?

indicators.note: screening means surrounding or shielding, so blood surrounds the short word

parts.note: claret is old boxing slang for blood

explanation.surface: A medical instrument used to take blood for screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests a medical tool; it is a musical one. CLARET for blood is sporting slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument with a single reed.

clue.text: Swift creation placed beside lake, queer one

indicators.note: beside places the word for placed next to the other pieces

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps
queer has an old British sense of feeling unwell, ill
I is the Roman numeral one
put means placed or set down

explanation.surface: Something set by a lake looks strange to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' is Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliput is the island of tiny people that Jonathan Swift invented in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Princess among cooler sultanas, exposing middle

parts.note: in means among
a fan cools you down

indicators.note: exposing middle means only the centre letters of sultanas are shown

explanation.surface: A princess eats sultanas in a cool drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese king, a princess.

clue.text: Slow advance in Civil War, Confederates in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Confederate troops move slowly as they fall back during the American Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters LWARC sit inside 'Civil War' and are read backwards; 'in' before 'Civil War' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to move forward very slowly, an advance at a snail's pace.

clue.text: Non-believer takes articles one way

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
I is the Roman numeral one
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A sceptic adopts one approach to articles of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist is a person who denies that any god exists.

clue.text: Recollection of Proust in state of unawareness

indicators.note: recollection read as re-collection, gathering the letters again in new order

explanation.surface: Remembering Proust sends one into a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Proust's novel of remembrance; 're-collection' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state of near-unconsciousness.

clue.text: Taken aback at fine cheese, fine stuff indeed!

indicators.note: taken aback means turned backwards, so the little word at is reversed

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil leads
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Someone surprised by an excellent cheese exclaims at its quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed!' is emphasis only; 'Taken aback' turns the little word at backwards. Stuff here means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous silk fabric, a fine material or stuff.

clue.text: One relaxing with puzzle, forgetting the time

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, so a letter is dropped from the puzzle

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone unwinding with a puzzle loses track of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An easer is something that eases or relaxes, one who slackens tension.

clue.text: Negative word I put in lower

indicators.note: put in tells us the letter goes inside the word for lower

parts.note: nether means lower, as in the nether regions

explanation.surface: A grammar note about placing a negative word lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Neither is used to deny both options, a negative like 'not either'.

clue.text: Underwear less than desirable

explanation.definitionFit: Pants are British underpants, and 'pants' is British slang for rubbish or poor quality.

clue.text: Classy line in what's often stood for monthly process

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the applause

parts.note: a standing ovation is applause people rise to their feet for
U is old British shorthand for upper-class

explanation.surface: A stylish line about something audiences stand for.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovulation is the release of an egg in the menstrual cycle, which happens about once a month.

clue.text: Second seizure behind the others

parts.note: rear means behind or at the back
the rest means the others or remainder

explanation.surface: A second fit strikes someone lagging behind the group.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrest someone is to take them into custody again, a second seizure by police.

clue.text: Printing term scored with former group

indicators.note: scored with means cut into, so the printer's word is split by the other piece

parts.note: stet is the proof-reader's mark meaning let it stand
ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A printer's word crossed out by a former band member.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six, especially musicians.
